qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A noodle-pulling technique has been prized in one mountain village for three generations. Within the village it never sits still — masters trade refinements over tea, apprentices carry tricks between the village's five noodle houses, and every family kitchen has its own variation. But cooks who marry outward are sworn to keep it secret, and to this day no restaurant beyond the village serves it. What does this story best illustrate?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: The invention of a brand-new cooking technique
The diffusion of a technique across regions and cultures
The circulation of a technique within a single community
The regulation of restaurant kitchens by inspectors

qti-content-body.p: Right. The technique moves constantly, between masters, apprentices, and the village's five noodle houses, but never past the village's edge. Lively movement that stays within one community is circulation.

Not quite. Two facts sit side by side here: the technique moves all the time, and it never leaves the village. Nothing new is created, no inspectors appear, and nothing spreads to the wider world. Pick the answer for movement inside a single community.

An invention would mean something brand-new is created in this story, but the technique has been in the village for three generations; what we watch is how it moves among the people who already have it. Name that constant local movement.

Diffusion carries something far beyond where it started, spreading it gradually until it is widely present across regions and cultures. This technique moves busily, which makes diffusion tempting, but it never crosses the village line: departing cooks are sworn to secrecy, and no outside restaurant serves it. Movement that stays inside one community is circulation, not diffusion.

Regulation would mean rules imposed by inspectors on restaurant kitchens, and no inspector or rule book appears anywhere in this story. The secrecy vow guards a local treasure; it doesn't police an industry. Find the answer for the technique's lively movement within the village.
